extracted.intended_audience: operators and managers of community public water systems; state/tribal primacy agencies and compliance officers
extracted.subtask_description: Regulatory requirements for public water systems on monitoring, compliance calculations, corrective action/notification, reporting to States, and Consumer Confidence Report content — with special emphasis on disinfection byproducts (TTHM, HAA5, bromate, chlorite), disinfectant residuals, TOC/DBP precursor controls, and enhanced coagulation/softening requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTHM and HAA5 compliance calculation (quarterly monitoring)
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems monitoring quarterly, compliance with MCLs in §141.64 must be based on a running annual arithmetic average, computed quarterly, of quarterly arithmetic averages of all samples collected by the system as prescribed by §141.132(b)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the running annual arithmetic average of quarterly averages covering any consecutive four‑quarter period exceeds the MCL, the system is in violation and must notify the public pursuant to §141.32 or §141.202 and report to the State pursuant to §141.134.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTHM and HAA5 compliance when monitoring < quarterly
rubrics_metrics.description: For systems monitoring less frequently than quarterly, systems demonstrate MCL compliance if the average of samples taken that year under §141.132(b)(1) does not exceed the MCL.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If that annual average exceeds the MCL the system must increase monitoring to once per quarter per treatment plant; such a system is not in violation until it has completed one year of quarterly monitoring unless fewer than four quarters of monitoring would cause the running annual average to exceed the MCL. Systems increasing to quarterly must calculate compliance including the sample which triggered increased monitoring plus the following three quarters.

rubrics_metrics.name: TTHM and HAA5 incomplete monitoring handling
rubrics_metrics.description: If a PWS fails to complete four consecutive quarters of monitoring, compliance with the MCL for the last four‑quarter compliance period must be based on an average of the available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Bromate compliance calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance must be based on a running annual arithmetic average, computed quarterly, of monthly samples (or the average of multiple samples in a month) collected as prescribed by §141.132(b)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the average of samples covering any consecutive four‑quarter period exceeds the MCL, the system is in violation and must notify the public pursuant to subpart Q and report to the State per §141.134. If a PWS fails to complete 12 consecutive months' monitoring, compliance for the last four‑quarter period is based on available data.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorite compliance (three-sample set average)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance must be based on an arithmetic average of each three sample set taken in the distribution system as prescribed by §141.132(b)(2)(i)(B) and §141.132(b)(2)(ii).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the arithmetic average of any three‑sample set exceeds the MCL, the system is in violation of the MCL and must notify the public pursuant to subpart Q and report to the State pursuant to §141.134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine and chloramines MRDL compliance calculation
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance must be based on a running annual arithmetic average, computed quarterly, of monthly averages of all samples collected under §141.132(c)(1).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If the average covering any consecutive four‑quarter period exceeds the MRDL, the system is in violation and must notify the public pursuant to subpart Q and report to the State pursuant to §141.134. When systems switch between chlorine and chloramines during the year, include all monitoring results together in calculating compliance and clearly indicate in reports which residual disinfectant was analyzed for each sample.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine dioxide acute violation criteria
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance is based on consecutive daily samples under §141.132(c)(2). If any daily sample at the entrance to the distribution system exceeds the MRDL and on the following day one or more of the three distribution system samples exceed the MRDL, the system is in violation and must take immediate corrective action and notify the public pursuant to the procedures for acute health risks in subpart Q and report to the State pursuant to §141.134.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to take distribution system samples the day following an exceedance at the entrance is also considered an MRDL violation and triggers public notification and State reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Chlorine dioxide nonacute violation and monitoring obligations
rubrics_metrics.description: If any two consecutive daily samples taken at the entrance to the distribution system exceed the MRDL and all distribution system samples taken are below the MRDL, the system is in violation (nonacute) and must take corrective action, notify the public per nonacute procedures in subpart Q, and report to the State per §141.134.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Failure to monitor at the entrance the day after an exceedance is also an MRDL violation and requires notification under the nonacute provisions (including §141.32(e)(78)) and State reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: DBP precursor (DBPP) compliance determination and Step 2 eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance for DBPP must be determined as specified by §141.135(c). Systems may begin monitoring up to 12 months prior to the compliance date but monitoring during that period is not required; failure to monitor then is not a violation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: However, a system that did not monitor in that prior period and subsequently determines in the first 12 months after the compliance date that it cannot meet Step 1 and must apply for Step 2 is not eligible for retroactive approval of Step 2. Systems may apply for Step 2 any time after the compliance date. For systems required to meet Step 1 TOC removals, if the value calculated under §141.135(c)(1)(iv) is less than 1.00, the system is in violation of the treatment technique and must notify the public pursuant to subpart Q and report to the State pursuant to §141.134.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reporting deadlines to State for sampling results (§141.134(a))
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems required to sample quarterly or more frequently must report to the State within 10 days after the end of each quarter in which samples were collected. Systems sampling less frequently than quarterly must report within 10 days after the end of each monitoring period in which samples were collected.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This reporting requirement is notwithstanding the provisions of §141.31.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reporting elements for disinfection byproducts (TTHM, HAA5, chlorite, bromate)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems must report, depending on monitoring frequency, items such as: number of samples in last period; location, date, and result of each sample; arithmetic average of samples in the last quarter or year; annual arithmetic average of quarterly arithmetic averages for the last four quarters; and whether, based on §141.133, the MCL was violated.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific requirements vary by contaminant and monitoring frequency (e.g., chlorite requires monthly entry point sample counts for last 3 months and per‑three‑sample‑set distribution averages). The State may choose to perform calculations and determine whether the MCL was exceeded in lieu of system reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reporting elements for disinfectants (chlorine, chloramines, chlorine dioxide)
rubrics_metrics.description: For chlorine/chloramines: number of samples taken during each month of last quarter; month arithmetic average for each month for last 12 months; arithmetic average of monthly averages for last 12 months; and whether the MRDL was violated per §141.133(c)(1). For chlorine dioxide: dates, results, and locations of samples taken during last quarter; whether MRDL was violated; and whether the MRDL was exceeded in any two consecutive daily samples and whether the violation was acute or nonacute.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The State may choose to perform calculations and determine whether the MRDL was exceeded in lieu of system reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required reporting elements for DBPP and enhanced coagulation/softening monitoring
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems monitoring monthly or quarterly for TOC and required to meet enhanced coagulation/softening must report: number of paired (source and treated) samples taken during the last quarter; location/date/results of each paired sample and associated alkalinity; monthly arithmetic average percent reduction of TOC for each paired sample and required TOC percent removal; calculations for determining compliance per §141.135(c)(1); and whether the system is in compliance with enhanced coagulation/softening percent removal requirements for the last four quarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For systems meeting alternative compliance criteria there are additional running annual averages and metrics to report (source/treatment TOC, SUVA, alkalinity, TTHM/HAA5, magnesium hardness removal, etc.). The State may perform the calculations in lieu of system reporting.

rubrics_metrics.name: Applicability of enhanced coagulation/enhanced softening (§141.135(a)(1))
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H systems using conventional filtration treatment must operate with enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening to achieve the TOC percent removal levels specified in paragraph (b) unless the system meets at least one of the alternative compliance criteria in paragraph (a)(2) or (a)(3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems must still comply with monitoring requirements in §141.132(d) even if relying on alternative criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criterion: source water TOC < 2.0 mg/L (a)(2)(i)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system's source water TOC level, measured according to §141.131(d)(3), is less than 2.0 mg/L, calculated quarterly as a running annual average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting this condition are not required to operate with enhanced coagulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criterion: treated water TOC < 2.0 mg/L (a)(2)(ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system's treated water TOC level, measured according to §141.131(d)(3), is less than 2.0 mg/L, calculated quarterly as a running annual average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting this condition are not required to operate with enhanced coagulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criterion: source TOC <4.0 mg/L with alkalinity >60 and low DBP or financial_commitment (a)(2)(iii)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system's source water TOC level is less than 4.0 mg/L (running annual average); source water alkalinity > 60 mg/L (CaCO3), and either the TTHM and HAA5 running annual averages are no greater than 0.040 mg/L and 0.030 mg/L respectively, or prior to the compliance effective date the system made a clear and irrevocable financial commitment to install technologies to limit TTHMs and HAA5 to those levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If relying on financial commitment, the system must submit evidence plus schedule/milestones to the State for approval and install/operate technologies by the approved date; failure to do so constitutes a violation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criterion: low TTHM/HAA5 and chlorine-only disinfection (a)(2)(iv)
rubrics_metrics.description: The TTHM and HAA5 running annual averages are no greater than 0.040 mg/L and 0.030 mg/L respectively, and the system uses only chlorine for primary disinfection and maintenance of a residual in the distribution system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting this condition are not required to operate with enhanced coagulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criterion: source water SUVA ≤ 2.0 L/mg-m (a)(2)(v)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system's source water SUVA, prior to any treatment and measured monthly according to §141.131(d)(4), is ≤ 2.0 L/mg‑m, calculated quarterly as a running annual average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting this condition are not required to operate with enhanced coagulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criterion: finished water SUVA ≤ 2.0 L/mg-m (a)(2)(vi)
rubrics_metrics.description: The system's finished water SUVA, measured monthly according to §141.131(d)(4), is ≤ 2.0 L/mg‑m, calculated quarterly as a running annual average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting this condition are not required to operate with enhanced coagulation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Alternative compliance criteria for softening systems (a)(3)(i-ii)
rubrics_metrics.description: Softening systems that cannot achieve Step 1 TOC removals may use: (i) softening that lowers treated water alkalinity to < 60 mg/L (CaCO3), measured monthly and calculated quarterly as a running annual average; or (ii) softening that removes at least 10 mg/L of magnesium hardness (as CaCO3), measured monthly and calculated quarterly as a running annual average.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting these alternative softening criteria are not required to operate with enhanced softening per paragraph (b)(2) table.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required Step 1 TOC reductions table (percent removals) (b)(2)
rubrics_metrics.description: Step 1 required removal of TOC by enhanced coagulation/enhanced softening is based on source-water TOC (ranges) and source-water alkalinity categories (0–60; >60–120; >120 mg/L as CaCO3), with specified percent removal targets (e.g., for source TOC >2.0–4.0: 35%, 25%, 15% respectively; higher TOC requires higher percent removal).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems meeting any condition in (a)(2)(i)-(vi) are not required to operate with enhanced coagulation. Softening systems meeting (a)(3) alternatives are not required to operate with enhanced softening. Systems practicing softening must meet the TOC removal requirements in the specified column.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 (alternate minimum TOC removal) application and timing (b)(3)
rubrics_metrics.description: Subpart H conventional treatment systems that cannot achieve Step 1 TOC removals due to water quality or operational constraints must apply to the State within three months of failure to achieve the TOC removals for approval of alternative minimum TOC (Step 2) removal requirements.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Until the State approves Step 2, the system must meet the Step 1 TOC removals in paragraph (b)(2). If the State approves alternate Step 2 requirements, the State may make those retroactive for compliance determination.

rubrics_metrics.name: Step 2 application testing requirements (bench/pilot) (b)(4)(i-v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Applications for Step 2 must include bench‑ or pilot‑scale testing results using representative water samples and adding 10 mg/L increments of alum (or equivalent ferric salt) to determine the alternate enhanced coagulation level: the dose/pH at which an incremental 10 mg/L alum addition results in a TOC removal of ≤ 0.3 mg/L; that percent removal at this point defines the minimum TOC removal for the system.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Testing must continue in 10 mg/L increments until the pH is reduced to the Step 2 target pH (table). For alkalinities <60 mg/L where small alum additions drop pH below 5.5 before TOC removal occurs, maintain pH between 5.3–5.7 in samples until TOC removal of 0.3 mg/L per 10 mg/L alum is reached. The system may operate at any coagulant dose or pH necessary (consistent with other NPDWRs) to achieve the approved minimum. If TOC removal is consistently <0.3 mg/L per 10 mg/L alum at all dosages, the water is deemed not amenable to enhanced coagulation and the system may apply for a waiver of enhanced coagulation requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Enhanced coagulation Step 2 target pH table
rubrics_metrics.description: Bench/pilot testing target pH values depend on alkalinity (mg/L as CaCO3): alkalinity 0–60 target pH 5.5; >60–120 target pH 6.3; >120–240 target pH 7.0; >240 target pH 7.5.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: For low alkalinity (<60), additional pH control instructions apply (maintain 5.3–5.7 when necessary).

rubrics_metrics.name: TOC compliance calculation method (c)(1)(i-v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems calculate compliance quarterly after collecting 12 months of data: (i) determine actual monthly TOC percent removal = (1 − (treated water TOC / source water TOC)) × 100; (ii) determine required monthly TOC percent removal from the table or Step 2; (iii) divide actual by required; (iv) add the results for the last 12 months and divide by 12; (v) if the resulting value is less than 1.00 the system is not in compliance with TOC percent removal requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Allowances to assign monthly value of 1.0 for TOC compliance (c)(2)(i-v)
rubrics_metrics.description: Systems may assign a monthly value of 1.0 (in lieu of the calculated ratio) for TOC compliance in specified circumstances: (i) any month treated or source water TOC <2.0 mg/L; (ii) any month a softening system removes ≥10 mg/L magnesium hardness; (iii) any month source water SUVA ≤2.0 L/mg‑m prior to treatment; (iv) any month finished water SUVA ≤2.0 L/mg‑m; (v) any month an enhanced softening system lowers alkalinity below 60 mg/L (CaCO3).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: These provisions may be used in lieu of the calculations in paragraph (c)(1) to determine compliance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Treatment techniques identified for DBP precursors (d)
rubrics_metrics.description: The Administrator identifies enhanced coagulation or enhanced softening as treatment techniques to control the level of disinfection byproduct precursors in Subpart H conventional treatment and distribution systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Purpose and applicability of Consumer Confidence Reports (§141.151)
rubrics_metrics.description: This subpart establishes minimum requirements for content of reports community water systems must deliver to customers. Reports must contain information on water quality and characterize risks (if any) from exposure to detected contaminants in an accurate and understandable manner. Systems serving more than 100,000 must develop and annually update a plan to assist consumers with limited English proficiency.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This subpart applies only to community water systems. 'Customers' are billing units/service connections; 'consumers' are people served including non‑billed persons. 'Detected' is defined with cross‑references to contaminant-specific detection thresholds. Primacy agencies may adopt alternative requirements by rule that provide equivalent information and public education.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Report timing and delivery (§141.152)
rubrics_metrics.description: Compliance dates: between June 24, 2024 and Dec 31, 2026 systems must comply with §§141.151–141.155 as codified July 1, 2023; later dates update sections. Each existing community water system must deliver reports by July 1 each year containing data collected during the previous calendar year (or most recent calendar year before previous). New systems must deliver first report by July 1 of year after first full calendar year in operation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Systems that sell water must deliver applicable information to buyer systems by specified dates or contractually agreed dates; special provisions exist for biannual reporting buyer systems.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Report: source of water information (§141.153(b))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report must identify source(s) of water by providing the type (surface water, ground water) and the commonly used name (if any) and location of the body(ies) of water.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If a source water assessment has been completed, the report must notify consumers of its availability, year completed/updated, and how to obtain it. Systems are encouraged to highlight significant contamination sources if readily available. If the primacy agency provided an assessment, include a brief summary of system susceptibility using language provided by the primacy agency or written by the operator.

rubrics_metrics.name: Consumer Confidence Report required definitions (§141.153(c))
rubrics_metrics.description: Each report must include definitions such as: Maximum Contaminant Level Goal (MCLG); Maximum Contaminant Level (MCL); Contaminant. Reports for systems operating under a variance or exemption must include the definition 'Variances and Exemptions'. Reports containing certain regulated terms must include definitions for Treatment Technique, Action Level, MRDLG, MRDL, and Hazard Index (HI).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reports that include Level 1/Level 2 Assessments must include definitions for those assessments. Systems must use specified definitions for Pesticide and Herbicide unless State‑approved alternate definitions are provided in writing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Presentation and data timeframe for detected contaminants (§141.153(d)(1-3))
rubrics_metrics.description: Data for contaminants subject to mandatory monitoring must be presented clearly and understandably (e.g., in one table or adjacent tables). Data must be derived from monitoring and analytical requirements during the previous calendar year, or the most recent calendar year before the previous, except where monitoring is allowed less often than once/year.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If monitoring less often than annually, include date and results of most recent sampling and a brief statement that the data are from the most recent testing done in accordance with regulations. No data older than 5 years need be included.

rubrics_metrics.name: Required contaminant data elements for detected regulated contaminants (§141.153(d)(4))
rubrics_metrics.description: For each detected regulated contaminant listed in appendix A: (i) the MCL for that contaminant (expressed as a number ≥1.0); (ii) the MCLG in same units; (iii) if no MCL, indicate applicable treatment technique or action level and include definitions; (iv) for MCL contaminants (except turbidity and E. coli), include the highest contaminant level used to determine compliance and the range of detected levels, with specific rules depending on how compliance is determined.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: When compliance is determined annually or less frequently: report highest detected level at any sampling point and range. When compliance is determined by running annual average at a monitoring location: report highest average of any monitoring location and range of individual sample results for all monitoring locations. For TTHM/HAA5, include highest locational running annual average and range of individual sample results for all monitoring locations; if multiple locations exceed the MCL, include locational running annual averages for all locations that exceed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Turbidity reporting specifics (§141.153(d)(4)(v))
rubrics_metrics.description: For turbidity: when reported pursuant to §141.13 include the highest average monthly value; when pursuant to §141.71 include the highest monthly value (and an explanation of why turbidity is measured); when pursuant to §§141.73/141.173/141.551 include the highest single measurement and the lowest monthly percentage of samples meeting turbidity limits and an explanation of why turbidity is measured.

rubrics_metrics.name: Lead and copper reporting specifics (§141.153(d)(4)(vi))
rubrics_metrics.description: For lead and copper: report the 90th percentile concentration of the most recent round(s) of sampling, the number of sampling sites exceeding the action level, and the range of tap sampling results.

rubrics_metrics.name: Include likely source(s) of detected contaminants (§141.153(d)(4)(ix))
rubrics_metrics.description: The contaminant data section(s) must include the likely source(s) of detected contaminants to the best of the operator's knowledge.
